title: Concatenate large_utf8 columns in mizu_arrow_col_utf8
description:
`mizu_arrow_col_utf8()` now also concatenates a null-free `large_utf8` column, narrowing its offsets to int32. Previously it declined, so a binding fell back to its per-element gather for every `large_string` producer.

`string_view` columns, columns with nulls, and columns past `INT32_MAX` bytes still decline.

title: Add a lazy Arrow open that defers the string walks
description:
Adds three binding-author functions to the Arrow frame writer:

* `mizu_arrow_open_lazy()` opens a frame without walking its string columns.
* `mizu_arrow_validate()` runs the deferred walks, skipping any column registered as a remote leaf.
* `mizu_arrow_size_floor()` gives a cheap lower bound on the region size, usable before the walks.

A binding can now register remote leaves before paying for the string walks, so a string column that crosses by reference is never walked. In mizu, an unchanged round trip of a 5M-row frame with a string column goes from 1.25 ms to 0.08 ms.

`mizu_arrow_open()` is unchanged.

title: Add mizu_pool_submit_wake and wake one worker per task in a batch submit
description:
Two changes to the batch submit's worker wake.

* New `mizu_pool_submit_wake()` (binding-author tier) exposes the batch submit's closing wake. A binding that abandons a batch midway and keeps the tasks already accepted calls it, so a parked worker is not left sleeping on them.

* A batch submit now wakes at most one idle worker per task. Previously a short batch woke every idle worker in the pool, and a worker whose wake was already in flight could be woken again for the same batch.

Measured through pymizu on an idle 8-worker pool, a one-task batch now wakes 1 worker rather than about 9, and the submit call drops from 48.5 to 20.7 us. Large-batch throughput is unchanged.

title: Refresh best-known benchmark figures
description:
Updates the README performance table and `bench/notes.md` with new bests from ten runs of `bench_channel` and `bench_pool` on 0.2.0. No code changes.

* Pool submit + collect drops to 0.2 µs (nil) and 0.8 µs (4 KiB), and the nil channel round trip to 0.2 µs.

* Pool task throughput now reads ~18 M tasks/s. This is the 1-worker row, which is now the highest of the three; the previous ~11 M was the 2-worker row.

The bests sit at the edge of wide run-to-run bands (the nil rows read about 0.33 µs in a typical run), so the notes entry records the min–max band for every row.

title: libmizu 0.2.0
description: Updates the declared library version to 0.2.0 and finalizes the 0.2.0 changelog. No wire ABI change is intended: the stable public header is unchanged since v0.1.0, so MIZU_ABI_VERSION stays at 1 and the soname major stays at 0.

title: Ship licensed release assets after full CI
description:
This makes two release-safety changes:

- Ships both license notices with the standalone amalgamation and includes them in its checksums.
- Runs the complete CI matrix at the tagged commit before publishing any release assets.

Validated with actionlint, ShellCheck, and the amalgamation smoke tests.

title: Fold duplicated collect wait, region open and notify arm paths
description:
Removes three pieces of duplicated code in the core. No behaviour or API change.

* `mizu_pool_collect_any()` and `mizu_pool_collect_all()` now share one wait loop. The loop is force-inlined with a constant predicate choice, so neither verb gains a branch or an indirect call.
* The three POSIX region-open forms share one helper for the name, open, size and map steps. Each keeps its own post-map advice.
* The channel and pool notify arms share one helper for the arm-time drain and the announce.

Also drops two channel fields that were written but never read.

The unit, ext-surface and integration tests pass, and the export list is unchanged. The pymizu and mizu benchmarks show no regression with this vendored.

title: Add Arrow column validity and utf8 concat exports
description:
Adds two binding-author exports for building a column from a chunked Arrow input without a per-row walk:

* `mizu_arrow_col_validity()` concatenates a column's validity bitmap across batches and returns its null count.
* `mizu_arrow_col_utf8()` concatenates a null-free utf8 column as rebased int32 offsets and packed bytes, with one copy per batch. It returns -1 for any other shape, so the caller keeps its per-element gather.

Also documents that `mizu_cvt_convert()` accepts a `NULL` `warn`, which skips the sentinel counting.

title: Speed up Arrow sentinel fills and validity rebuild
description:
Follow-up to #6, with further speedups to Arrow null handling.

* All-null runs fill about three times faster (five times for dictionary columns).

* Writing a frame from several batches, or from a sliced batch, rebuilds the validity bitmap 10-35x faster. The two-batch frame write is 24-30% faster overall.

* Unknown null counts on a sliced batch now resolve as fast as on an unsliced one, and conversions of sliced batches with nulls load validity a word at a time.

`test_bitmap_differential` covers the new paths, and `bench/notes.md` has the numbers.

title: Speed up Arrow open and null handling
description:
Follow-up to #5 with four more speedups in the Arrow writer, each measured with `bench_arrow` (8M rows, Apple M4 Pro).

* Opening a frame with a dictionary column is about 3x faster (1.4 ms to 0.4 ms), and no longer depends on how many nulls the column has.

* Resolving an unknown null count at open is about 12x faster (0.15 ms to 0.01 ms).

* Converting a column where around half the values are null is 17-33% faster.

* Writing a frame made of several batches, or of sliced batches, is about 3x faster when the columns contain nulls (6.0 ms to 1.9 ms at 1% nulls).

Null-free and sparse-null conversions are unchanged, within run-to-run noise.

Also adds tests for sparse-null conversion, dictionary validation across large batches, and the rebuilt validity bitmap, plus a whole-frame row in `bench_arrow`. Records are in `bench/notes.md`.

title: Speed up Arrow conversion kernels
description:
Speeds up Arrow columns with scattered nulls, dictionary columns, and date/timestamp conversions. Unknown null counts now use word-wise counting, and opening narrow frames allocates less.

Wire bytes and the exported API are unchanged. Adds differential tests and a report-only kernel benchmark.

title: Batch collect verb and one-slot large-region cache
description:
- Adds `mizu_pool_collect_terminal` to the ext tier: a batch collect for event-driven drains that claims every terminal task in a set in one call, never parks, skips tasks still in flight, and stops at the first per-item failure with the consumed prefix returned. pymizu's executor drain and asyncio pump adopt it; the mizu R package follows on re-vendor.
- Retains one over-cap spill region per handle: repeated sends of a payload larger than 64 MB now reuse the region instead of creating a fresh shared-memory region per send (~4x on pymizu's frame relay row).
- Simplifies the batch collect's per-item pre-checks to a single atomic load and drops the free-list scan for over-cap pops, which the insert gate makes a provable miss.

title: Speed up masked Arrow conversions and large view reads on Linux
description:
Tuning pass from a Linux benchmark baseline against the M4 Pro records, where masked Arrow staging ran 7-8x off the identity row.

- Consecutive all-valid or all-null words of a masked column's validity bitmap now convert as one run, so large masked columns take the same bulk-copy path as unmasked ones.
- The int32/int64 sentinel count fuses into the copy loop (int64 below 16 MiB keeps the previous two-pass form, which measures faster there).
- View opens past 1 MiB prefault their pages on Linux, so a large zero-copy payload's first read no longer faults page by page.

Measured on the Linux host (i7-1165G7): masked float64 staging 704 -> 344 us, masked int64 816 -> 636 us, masked+scan int32 ~300 -> 188 us.

title: Point license badge at absolute URL so doxygen renders the link
description:
Doxygen can't resolve the relative `LICENSE` target, so the mainpage shows the badge's raw markdown. Linking the absolute GitHub URL renders the badge as a link, matching the other badges.

Closes #1.
